newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn gains 12-cent limit on drier weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn gains 12-cent limit on drier weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply higher and up the 12-cent-per-bushel limit in the December through July contracts on hotter, drier weather over the weekend in the U.S. Midwest and indications that pattern may continue this week, traders said.
"The fact is, we didn't get the central Illinois rain and the perception is there may be some kind of a change in the pattern," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp.
Meteorologists said hot, dry conditions are expected to continue for at least five days in pockets of Illinois, Iowa and Missouri, which may stress the corn crop during its pollination period.

"For the next five days, we will see dry conditions in the dry areas of western Illinois and extreme southeastern Iowa," said Kevin Marcus, agricultural meteorologist and director of CROPCAST Services Marketing in Rockville, Md.
The corn crop is in its pollination stage and would benefit from warm, not hot weather and showers of 0.5 to 1.0 inch or more.
Corn closed 5-3/4 to 12 cents up, with September up 11-3/4 at $2.48-1/2. December was up the 12-cent limit at $2.49.

Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for normal to above normal temperatures in the western portion of the U.S. Midwest from July 17 to July 22. Normal to below normal temperatures were forecast for the eastern growing region. The outlook also predicted rainfall to be mostly normal to above normal in the Midwest. The exception was Nebraska and western Iowa where below normal rain was seen.

Iowa Grain bought eight million bushels of December, LIT America bought 10.0 million December and sold four million, Griffin Trading bought three million December, R.J. O'Brien bought five million December and Rand Financial bought five million December, traders said.
Prudential Securities sold ten million December and SAK Futures sold five million while Cargill Inc sold three million, traders said.
In spread trading Cargill Inc did 1.5 million December/July at 13-1/2 cents and LFG Futures did 1.5 million September/December at even money to 1/2 cent, premium December, floor sources said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 67,000 contracts, above the 47,677 traded Friday.

In corn options, LIT America sold 500 December $3.10 calls at 1-3/4 to two cents and sold 500 September $2.70 calls at four cents, traders said. Smith Barney sold 500 December $3.20 calls at two cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, above the 16,884 traded Friday.
